issues.description: In ex5_grover_kakuro.py, the template sets `self.number_of_qubits_query_register` to a float (`0.0`), but `QuantumRegister(...)` requires an integer number of qubits. This will raise an error when constructing `QuantumRegister(self.number_of_qubits_query_register, ...)`, preventing students from instantiating `GroverKakuro` and running any part of Exercise 5. The reference solution uses an integer (`4`).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template attribute initialization to an integer: `self.number_of_qubits_query_register = 0` (or set it directly to `4` to match the exercise), so `QuantumRegister(...)` receives an int.

issues.description: Exercises 2.6/4.6/5.6 require returning measurement counts, but the reference solutions use `Aer.get_backend("statevector_simulator")` and then call `result.get_counts(qc)`. Counts are intended for shot-based measurement simulators (e.g., `qasm_simulator`), and `get_counts` is not consistently supported/meaningful for the statevector simulator across Qiskit versions. This creates a mismatch between the problem statement (counts) and the simulation approach used, risking runtime errors or confusing students about which backend to use.
issues.suggestedFix: For count-based exercises, switch to `Aer.get_backend("qasm_simulator")` (keep measurements and use `execute(..., shots=...)`), and keep returning `result.get_counts(qc)`. Alternatively, if keeping `statevector_simulator`, return a statevector/probability distribution instead and update the problem statement/tests accordingly.

issues.description: The QFT exercises are numbered as Exercise 6 in the problem statement, but the corresponding code file and docstrings are labeled as Exercise 1 (file `ex1_qft.py`, docstrings say “Exercise 1.1/1.2”). This naming/numbering mismatch makes it non-obvious for students that Exercise 6 should be implemented in `ex1_qft.py` and can lead them to search for an `ex6_*.py` file or “Exercise 6” markers in code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align identifiers by updating `ex1_qft.py` docstrings to reference “Exercise 6.1/6.2” (and optionally rename the file/class to `ex6_qft.py` / similar if tests/imports allow).

issues.description: The QFT-for-N-qubits exercises are numbered as Exercise 7 in the problem statement, but the corresponding code file and docstrings are labeled as Exercise 2 (file `ex2_qft.py`, docstrings say “Exercise 2.1/2.2”). This inconsistency makes it harder to map Exercise 7 instructions to the correct implementation location.
issues.suggestedFix: Update `ex2_qft.py` docstrings to “Exercise 7.1/7.2” (or rename the file to `ex7_qft.py` if the surrounding tooling/tests can be updated).
